Let $B$ be the event that a teenager started to play music before $6$ years old, $M$ be the event that a teenager is good at math, and ${T}_{1},{T}_{2},{T}_{3}$ be the events that a teenager plays piano, violin, or another instrument, respectively. 

Let's break down the information given in the problem statement:

- From the bullet points, we have the following information:

$$
\begin{aligned} & P({T}_{1})=0.2 &  & P(M|{T}_{1})=0.6 \\  & P({T}_{2})=0.15 \\  & P({T}_{3})=0.65 &  & P(M|{T}_{3})=0.35\end{aligned}
$$

The disjoint union ${T}_{1}⊔{T}_{2}⊔{T}_{3}$ covers the entire sample space, and we have

$$
P({T}_{1})+P({T}_{2})+P({T}_{3})=0.2+0.15+0.65=1.
$$

- Since $12%$ of teenagers started to play before $6$ years old, we have

$$
P(B)=0.12.
$$

- Since $27%$ of teenagers who started to play before $6$ years old are good at math, we have

$$
P(M|B)=0.27.
$$

- Since $8%$ of students who are good at math started to play an instrument before $6$ years old, we have

$$
P(B|M)=0.08.
$$

We want to find the probability that a randomly chosen teenager who plays the violin is good at math, which is represented as $P(M|{T}_{2}).$ 

Using Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(B|M) & =\frac{P(M|B)P(B)}{P(M)} \\ P(B|M) & =\frac{P(M|B)P(B)}{P(M|{T}_{1})P({T}_{1})+P(M|{T}_{2})P({T}_{2})+P(M|{T}_{3})P({T}_{3})} \\ 0.08 & =\frac{(0.27)(0.12)}{(0.2)(0.6)+P(M|{T}_{2})(0.15)+(0.35)(0.65)} \\ 0.08 & =\frac{0.0324}{0.3475+0.15P(M|{T}_{2})}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this equation for $P(M|{T}_{2}),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}0.08(0.3475+0.15P(M|{T}_{2})) & =0.0324 \\ 0.3475+0.15P(M|{T}_{2}) & =\frac{0.0324}{0.08} \\ 0.3475+0.15P(M|{T}_{2}) & =\frac{81}{200} \\ 0.15P(M|{T}_{2}) & =\frac{81}{200}-0.3475 \\ P(M|{T}_{2}) & =\frac{1}{0.15}(\frac{81}{200}-0.3475) \\ P(M|{T}_{2}) & ≈0.383\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.

Let B be the event that a teenager started to play music before 6 years old, M be the event that a teenager is good at math, and T1,T2,T3 be the events that a teenager plays piano, violin, or another instrument, respectively.

Let's break down the information given in the problem statement:

  • From the bullet points, we have the following information: P(T1)=0.2P(M|T1)=0.6P(T2)=0.15P(T3)=0.65P(M|T3)=0.35 The disjoint union T1⊔T2⊔T3 covers the entire sample space, and we have P(T1)+P(T2)+P(T3)=0.2+0.15+0.65=1.

  • Since 12% of teenagers started to play before 6 years old, we have P(B)=0.12.

  • Since 27% of teenagers who started to play before 6 years old are good at math, we have P(M|B)=0.27.

  • Since 8% of students who are good at math started to play an instrument before 6 years old, we have P(B|M)=0.08.

We want to find the probability that a randomly chosen teenager who plays the violin is good at math, which is represented as P(M|T2).

Using Bayes' theorem combined with the law of total probability, we have

P(B|M)=P(M|B)P(B)P(M)P(B|M)=P(M|B)P(B)P(M|T1)P(T1)+P(M|T2)P(T2)+P(M|T3)P(T3)0.08=(0.27)(0.12)(0.2)(0.6)+P(M|T2)(0.15)+(0.35)(0.65)0.08=0.03240.3475+0.15P(M|T2)

Solving this equation for P(M|T2), we have

0.08(0.3475+0.15P(M|T2))=0.03240.3475+0.15P(M|T2)=0.03240.080.3475+0.15P(M|T2)=812000.15P(M|T2)=81200−0.3475P(M|T2)=10.15(81200−0.3475)P(M|T2)≈0.383 rounded to three decimal places.
